problem: Given the function $f(x)={x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+12x-5,$ which of the following statements are true?
worked_solution:
First, we find the stationary points. Differentiating $f(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}-12x+12.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-12x+12 & =0 \\ 3({x}^{2}-4x+4) & =0 \\ 3(x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=2$ is the only stationary point of $f(x).$ Next, to determine whether this point is a local maximum or minimum, we use the first derivative test.

Let's choose the test points $x=0,3$ and evaluate the first derivative at these points.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =3(0)^{2}-12(0)+12=12>0 \\ {f}^{′}(3) & =3(3)^{2}-12(3)+12=3>0\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize the information in a table shown below.

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,2)$ | $2$ | $(2,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $0$ |  | $3$ |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $+$ |
| $f$ | $↗$ |  | $↗$ |

The first derivative does not change sign at $x=2.$ Therefore, we conclude that $x=2$ is neither a minimum nor a maximum.

Hence, the first derivative test shows that the function has no local extrema.

choices.value: There is a local minimum at $x=2$
There is a local maximum at $x=0$
There is a local minimum at $x=0$
The function $f(x)$ has no local extrema
There is a local maximum at $x=2$
